ETH Zurich Library, probability historical exhibit
Stephen M. Stigler (2015), Cardano dice counts

claims.statement: Galileo's Sopra le scoperte dei dadi is represented in Opere vol.8 (1898) pp.591-594
claims.caution: Exact original manuscript year not asserted

claims.statement: Galileo treated three-dice sums 9/12 versus 10/11 and observed equal unordered types but differing multiplicities
Unordered representations of sums 9 and 10 number six each but ordered outcome counts are 25 and 27
Three independent fair dice have 216 equally likely ordered results and probabilities 25/216 vs 27/216
claims.caution: Not automatically the frequency in any fixed number of trials

claims.statement: Replacing each face x by 7-x gives a bijection between sum s and 21-s
Pre-Galileo three-dice counts are documented in medieval text traditions
216 trials have expected counts 25 and 27 for sums 9 and 10, not guaranteed realized frequencies
